title: THE AIR FORCE ACT, 1950
long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the government of the Air Force.

sections.text: This Act may be called the Air Force Act, 1950. It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may by notification appoint.
Lists the categories of persons subject to this Act, including officers, warrant officers, airmen, and certain other persons connected with the Air Force.

sections.section_title: Termination of application of the Act
sections.text: Provides for the circumstances in which the application of the Act to a person terminates.

Defines key terms used in the Act including active service, Air Force, Air Force custody, Chief of the Air Staff, commanding officer, court-martial, enemy, officer, prescribed, superior officer, and other related expressions.

chapters.chapter_title: SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR THE APPLICATION OF ACT IN CERTAIN CASES

sections.section_title: Application of Act to certain forces under the Central Government
sections.text: The Central Government may apply the Act to any force raised and maintained in India under the authority of that Government.

sections.section_title: Special provision as to rank in certain cases
sections.text: Provides for determination of rank of persons subject to the Act in special circumstances.

sections.section_title: Commanding Officer of person subject to Air Force law under clause (d) of section 2
sections.text: Specifies who is the commanding officer for certain categories of persons.

sections.section_title: Officers exercising powers in certain cases
sections.text: Provides for officers who may exercise powers under the Act in certain situations.

sections.section_title: Power to declare persons to be on active service
sections.text: The Central Government may declare that any person or class of persons subject to the Act shall be on active service.
Provides for the grant of commissions and appointments in the Air Force.
No person who is not a citizen of India shall be enrolled in the Air Force except with the consent of the Central Government.

sections.section_title: Ineligibility of females for enrolment or employment
sections.text: No female shall be eligible for enrolment or employment in the Air Force except in such corps, units or other body and under such conditions as the Central Government may specify.
Prescribes the procedure before the enrolling officer, mode of enrolment, validity of enrolment, and related matters.
Deals with tenure of service, dismissal, removal, retirement, release, and other conditions of service of persons subject to the Act.
Provides for privileges of persons subject to the Act in respect of arrest, attachment of property, and other civil matters.

Defines various service offences including offences in relation to the enemy, mutiny, desertion, absence without leave, insubordination, neglect of duty, property offences, drunkenness, and other disciplinary offences, together with the punishments prescribed therefor.

Specifies the scale of punishments that may be awarded by courts-martial and by commanding officers, including death, imprisonment, dismissal, reduction in rank, forfeiture of seniority, fine, and other minor punishments.
Provides for deductions from pay and allowances on account of absence, imprisonment, fine, damage to property, and other causes.
Deals with arrest of offenders, custody, investigation of charges, and preparation for trial by court-martial.
Provides for the constitution, powers and procedure of general, district and summary general courts-martial, including the appointment of judge advocates and the rules of evidence and procedure.
Lays down detailed rules of procedure for the conduct of trials by courts-martial, including challenges, oaths, examination of witnesses, findings and sentences.

chapters.chapter_title: CONFIRMATION AND REVISION OF FINDINGS AND SENTENCES

sections.text: Provides for the confirmation of findings and sentences of courts-martial by the competent confirming authority, and for revision of findings and sentences.
Deals with the execution of sentences of death, imprisonment, dismissal and other punishments awarded by courts-martial.
Empowers the Central Government and other authorities to grant pardons, remit or commute sentences, and suspend the execution of sentences.
Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, including rules of procedure for courts-martial and other matters.
Provides for the continuance of proceedings and other transitional arrangements upon the coming into force of the Act.
